mechanism: Pull yearly NFP release timestamps from the Economic Calendar; on EURUSD M15 compare the release candle's high-low height to the candles one hour before and after; if the center candle is taller than both neighbors, mark an NFP volatility spike at that broker-clock time. Track when the spike consistently appears then suddenly vanishes (or shifts) across NFP dates; that flip window is matched against computed EU/US/AU DST start-end calendars to identify the broker's DST rule and recover base UTC offset from TimeTradeServer vs TimeGMT.
data_needed: CalendarValueHistory NFP dates for a year; EURUSD (or broker-suffixed) M15 OHLC; GetCandleHeight; IsCandleLargerThanSurrounding ±1h; GetEUDSTDates/GetUSDSTDates/GetAUDSTDates; IsInDSTRange with southern-hemisphere OR logic for AU; TimeTradeServer/TimeGMT offset.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD (EURUSDm, EURUSD.pro, EURUSD.a variants); M15 candles; NFP monthly first-Friday schedule; EU/US/AU DST calendars; sessions London/Tokyo/NY referenced for later use.
why_new_for_mis: Uses a scheduled high-impact event's brief M15 range spike as a clock fingerprint to sense broker DST/timezone regime—MIS can align session and calendar sensors to true session local time without trusting broker disclosures.
quote: For each NFP date, check whether the EURUSD M15 candle at that time shows a volatility spike. Track when the pattern flips, if NFP was consistently volatile at datetime X, then suddenly stops being volatile, the broker shifted their clock (DST transition happened).

mechanism: Maintain five Adaptive Moving Averages with different periods; form ten pairwise comparisons into a six-state trend label (strong up, up, weak up, weak down, down, strong down). Per timeframe emit that state, then aggregate across a configured timeframe group via signal-count majority vote (countmax) so the most-agreed Enum becomes the multi-TF consensus regime fed to nine AMA strategy maps (pure trend through aggressive swing reversal).
data_needed: Five AMA series per TF; pairwise comparison matrix; EStrategyType/entry-signal enums; CArrayList of ENUM_TIMEFRAMES in g_group; signalcounts vector and majority countmax.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Framework symbol-agnostic (forex/equity/commodity sessions discussed); multi-timeframe AMA group via g_group.TimeFrame; Period_Seconds average for stop-order expiry.
why_new_for_mis: Discrete six-state trend regime from multi-AMA pairwise consensus plus cross-TF majority—not a single crossover—gives MIS a graded trend-state sensor suitable for time-window conditioning.
quote: Instead of relying on a single crossover, the optimizer compares every AMA pair and converts the result into a six-state trend signal… CGroupSelectAMAs aggregates signals across multiple timeframes and outputs the most-agreed signal.

mechanism: SSessionTimezone metadata (baseUTCOffset, dstRule, session start/end) drives DST-aware conversion between session local time and broker server time. CIntradaySession then classifies the session into OPEN/MID/CLOSE phases by market type (continuous forex vs fixed equity hours) and IsSessionHourMatch gates trades on session type, hour offset, 15-minute mark, and DST-adjusted broker time—so e.g. only London open hour is tradable rather than the whole session.
data_needed: Session enums (London/Tokyo/NY etc.); DST_EU/US/AU rules; sessionStart/End hour-minute; market-type intraday configs; TimeTradeServer; IsSessionHourMatch inputs.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: London ~08:00–16:30 GMT/BST; Tokyo midnight–9am GMT; NY ~1pm–10pm GMT; equity open/mid/close templates; forex near-continuous week schedule.
why_new_for_mis: Session-phase regime (open vs mid vs close) under explicit DST conversion is a clock-aligned microstructure regime MIS can fuse with strategy performance by window.
quote: IntradaySession takes into account market type and session time zones to configure intraday sessions from open, mid to close… IsSessionHourMatch function verifies: session type, hour offset, 15-minute mark, DST-adjusted broker time.

mechanism: UpdateTimeData maps TimeTradeServer into STimeData buckets: month (EMonthOfYear), quarter ((mon-1)/3), weeks-of-month (floor((day-1)/7) capped at 3 so days 29–31 stay in week 4), biweekly half-month, trading day, hour, and minute marks 00/15/30/45. IsCalendarMatch filters whether current calendar matches a configured monochronic window (hour handled separately by session match) so one strategy is paired with one time compartment.
data_needed: TimeTradeServer → MqlDateTime; STimeData fields; input calendar configuration; IsCalendarMatch; EMinuteOfHour 00/15/30/45.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any broker symbol under TimeTradeServer; calendar granularity from quarter down to quarter-hour; series aims to optimize windows historically.
why_new_for_mis: Hierarchical calendar-state vector as a sensing feature—MIS can treat time-of-calendar as an explicit regime axis rather than a passive backtest filter.
quote: Rather than creating a trading expert to trade whenever a setup appears, in this series, we will incorporate time awareness to enter a trade when probabilities are favorable based on time and schedule patterns.

mechanism: Map recurring session-local activity: USDJPY most active Asian+NY; EURUSD peaks European+NY; gold notably volatile in London–NY overlap; equity indices concentrate moves at local open/close (US indices large swings at 9:30 ET and near 4:00 ET); oil reacts to 14:30 ET releases plus session patterns. Use these as prior volatility/liquidity rhythm sensors when choosing monochronic windows.
data_needed: Session boundaries in GMT/ET; symbol identity; overlap intervals; scheduled release clocks (e.g. 14:30 ET).
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: USD/JPY; EUR/USD; gold; U.S. equity indices; oil; session TF context (intraday hours), not a single chart period.
why_new_for_mis: Explicit instrument×session volatility rhythm priors—MIS can bias sensing/attention toward historically active session overlaps per asset class.
quote: USD/JPY is most active in Asian session and New York sessions, while EUR/USD peaks during European and New York sessions. Gold is notably volatile during New York and London sessions especially in the session overlap.

mechanism: Treat :00/:15/:30/:45 clock marks as event anchors because major releases/fixings cluster on the hour or half-hour (US data often :30 or on the hour; European often :00). Equity open microstructure: volume/volatility surge at 9:30 ET, elevated first minutes, common pullback/consolidation around 9:45 ET (~15 min after open) before trend resume—use quarter-hour filters as volatility-phase sensors.
data_needed: Server/session clock; EMinuteOfHour marks; equity open timestamp; short post-open window bars.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: U.S. equities around 9:30–9:45 ET; FX/macro around scheduled :00/:30 releases; minute-level marks inside sessions.
why_new_for_mis: Quarter-hour clock microstructure as a volatility-phase sensor—MIS can tag open-flurry vs :45 retrace vs release-aligned minutes without indicator buffers.
quote: volume and volatility surge at the 9:30 ET open… common for price to pull back around 9:45 ET (15 minutes after open) before resuming a trend.

mechanism: Part 6 of a Chart Trade RAD/UI series: extend MQL5 object IDE with read-only EDIT fields for symbol name and daily accumulated deal profit (HistorySelect + DEAL_PROFIT sum), color by sign, DispatchMessage/OnTrade wiring, and memMax cache to skip recomputation when deal count unchanged. No market regime, volatility, liquidity, or sequence sensing is built.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Current Terminal symbol; daily local-time deal history only (UI P&L display).
why_new_for_mis: UI/RAD library tutorial after full read; daily P&L label is operator chrome, not a market sensing idea for MIS.
quote: I will show the simplest and correct way to add functionality to our IDE… EDIT 00 object to receive the name of the asset… EDIT 01 object will receive the accumulated value for a certain period.
